content.value_statement: Plugin repositories need consistent structure, validation, and release steps. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code a focused guide for ANcpLua plugin work.
actual_capabilities: Explains the required plugin directory layout and manifest locations.
Points agents to conventions, publishing, and testing reference guides.
Lists validation commands for full repositories and single plugins.
Describes marketplace sync checks and release checklist items.
Summarizes common mistakes around paths, versions, and frontmatter.
limitations: It is tailored to the ANcpLua plugin monorepo.
It does not create plugin files by itself.
It relies on local validation scripts being present.
It does not replace official Claude Code documentation.

use_cases.title: Create a new plugin
use_cases.description: Follow the repository structure, manifest requirements, documentation steps, and validation flow before opening a change.

use_cases.title: Debug plugin validation
use_cases.description: Use the testing guide to check JSON syntax, permissions, paths, marketplace sync, and component behavior.

use_cases.title: Review a release update
use_cases.description: Compare version fields, changelog entries, README coverage, and validation results before publishing.

prompt_templates.title: Start a plugin
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me create a new plugin in this repository. Show the required folders, manifest fields, README needs, and validation steps.

prompt_templates.title: Update an existing plugin
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my planned plugin change against the repository conventions. Check paths, manifest placement, naming, and documentation requirements.

prompt_templates.title: Diagnose validation failure
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the testing guidance to investigate why this plugin validation fails. Prioritize JSON syntax, permissions, paths, and marketplace sync.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare publishing review
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this plugin for release readiness. Verify version consistency, changelog coverage, README accuracy, validation status, and convention compliance.

output_examples.input: Help me add a new plugin to the monorepo.
output: A setup checklist covering the plugin directory, manifest, README, changelog entry, and validation sequence.
Notes about using portable paths and placing assets outside the manifest directory.

output_examples.input: My plugin does not load in Claude Code.
output: A debugging plan that checks local validation, JSON syntax, executable permissions, hardcoded paths, and relevant application logs.
A short list of likely fixes based on the failed check.
A release readiness summary covering version alignment, marketplace sync, documentation, validation, and restart requirements.
A focused list of blockers and follow-up tasks.

best_practices: Keep plugin assets outside the manifest directory unless they are manifests.
Use portable plugin root variables for paths in configurations.
Run repository validation and marketplace sync checks before publishing.
anti_patterns: Placing skills, commands, agents, or hooks inside the manifest directory.
Using absolute user paths in plugin configuration.
Publishing with version mismatches between manifest and marketplace entries.

faq.question: What does this skill help with?
faq.answer: It guides plugin creation, modification, debugging, validation, and release preparation inside the ANcpLua plugin monorepo.

faq.question: Which tools can use it?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Does it run validation automatically?
faq.answer: No. It documents validation workflows and commands that an agent or user may run when appropriate.

faq.question: Is it useful outside this repository?
faq.answer: It can teach general plugin patterns, but many details are specific to the ANcpLua repository.

faq.question: What files does it emphasize?
faq.answer: It emphasizes plugin manifests, SKILL.md frontmatter, README files, changelog entries, and marketplace metadata.

faq.question: What should users verify before publishing?
faq.answer: Users should verify validation results, marketplace sync, version alignment, documentation accuracy, and required restart steps.
